An effect runs again only when something in its dependency array changes. If the effect reads a value that is missing from the array, it does not run when that value changes and keeps working with the old one. If the array lists a value the effect never reads, the effect runs more often than it has to.

This check comes from the React Compiler, which works out what each effect in a component or hook depends on and compares that with your array.

As `react-hooks/exhaustive-effect-dependencies` the rule reports nothing, because `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` leaves this check of the compiler switched off. It runs with an oxlint config, as `react/exhaustive-effect-dependencies`. Everywhere else, use `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`.

## Examples

Reported with an oxlint config:

{/* bad {"config": "oxlint"} */}
```jsx
import { useEffect } from "react";

function Room({ roomId }) {
  useEffect(() => {
    connect(roomId);
  }, []); // stays in the first room
}
```

{/* bad {"config": "oxlint"} */}
```jsx
import { useEffect } from "react";

function Room({ roomId, theme }) {
  useEffect(() => {
    connect(roomId);
  }, [roomId, theme]); // reconnects when the theme changes
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
import { useEffect } from "react";

function Room({ roomId }) {
  useEffect(() => {
    connect(roomId);
  }, [roomId]);
}
```
